\section*{Author's text: 1. Introduction}
% SOURCE physical 2, printed 47: beginning of Introduction.
Let $f:X\rat X$ be a rational map on a smooth projective surface over an
algebraically closed field. Studying $f$ as a dynamical system is complicated
by the fact that $f$ need not be continuously defined on all points of $X$.
For example a rational map $f$ induces a natural pullback operator on curves
$f^*:\Pic(X)\to\Pic(X)$, but this operator may not iterate well. We say
$f$ is algebraically stable iff $\forall n\in\mathbb N\ (f^*)^n=(f^n)^*$.
This is equivalent to the geometric condition that $f$ has no destabilising
orbits [13] [7, 1.14]; i.e. an orbit of (closed) points
$p,f(p),\ldots,f^{n-1}(p)$ in $X$, for which $f^{-1}(p)$ and
$f(f^{n-1}(p))$ are curves. It is natural to hope that blowing up the points
in such an orbit will improve the situation. The main theme of this paper
is to discuss the extent to which this actually works.

% SOURCE physical 3, printed 48.
Assume for the rest of the paper that all surfaces are projective varieties
over an algebraically closed field, and unless explicitly stated, also
smooth. We write $\phi:X\rat Y$ to indicate that $f$ is a rational map
between surfaces, and we use a solid arrow $f:X\to Y$ when $f$ is a morphism.

\sourcestatement{Definition 1.1}{We write $\phi:(g,Y)\rat(f,X)$ to indicate
that $\phi:Y\rat X$ is a birational map conjugating $f:X\rat X$ to
$g=\phi^{-1}\circ f\circ\phi:Y\rat Y$. When $g:Y\rat Y$ is algebraically
stable, we say that $\phi$ stabilises $f$.}

Diller--Favre [7] proved that for a birational map $(f,X)$ there is always
a birational morphism $\pi:(g,Y)\to(f,X)$ which stabilises $f$. Not all
(non-invertible) rational maps can be stabilised, however. Favre [9] showed
for example that many monomial maps on $\mathbb P^2$ cannot be stabilised by
any birational conjugacy. See also [18]; for discussion on monomial maps in
higher dimensions see [20, 21], and for the local case at normal surface
singularities see [10, 15].

Algebraic stability is valuable in particular because the first dynamical
degree becomes easy to compute. This can be defined by
\[
 \lambda_1(f)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\|(f^n)^*\|^{1/n}.
\]
For an $f:X\rat X$ which is not algebraically stable, this computation is
usually intractable. However, if one has a stabilisation
$\phi:(g,Y)\rat(f,X)$ then the first dynamical degree, which is birationally
invariant, can be computed simply as the spectral radius of $g^*$. This
also shows that rational maps which can be stabilised have a first dynamical
degree that is an algebraic integer. The recent work of Bell, Diller, and
Jonsson [4] gives an example of a rational map with transcendental first
dynamical degree, hence providing another rational map which could never
be stabilised.

In any case the arguments in Diller--Favre support the idea that blowing
up destabilising orbits is a good approach to achieving algebraic stability.
The evidence of various examples [1, 2, 3, 9] shows that this approach not
only succeeds in many cases but is practical to carry out explicitly.

Let us call a destabilising orbit minimal when it does not contain any
shorter ones.

\sourcestatement{Proposition 1.2}{Suppose that $f:X\rat X$ is a rational
map on a surface. Let $p,f(p),\ldots,f^{n-1}(p)$ be a minimal destabilising
orbit for $f$ and $\pi:X'\to X$ be the birational morphism blowing up each
$p_j=f^{j-1}(p)$. Then any birational morphism $\rho:(g,Y)\to(f,X)$
stabilising $(f,X)$ factors as $\rho=\pi\circ\nu$ for some birational
morphism $\nu:Y\to X'$.}

% SOURCE physical 4, printed 49: complete algorithm and main statement.
\sourceheading{Definition 1.3 (Minimal Stabilisation Algorithm)}
\textit{Given a rational surface map $f_0:X_0\rat X_0$ we define a
(possibly finite) sequence
$\pi_m:(f_{m+1},X_{m+1})\to(f_m,X_m)$ for $m\geq0$ as follows}
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \textit{If $f_m$ is algebraically stable, stop.}
 \item \textit{If not, then pick a minimal destabilising orbit
 $p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_n$ and blowup each of the $p_j$ to produce
 $\pi_m:(f_{m+1},X_{m+1})\to(f_m,X_m)$.}
\end{enumerate}
\textit{If this sequence terminates at $f_M:X_M\rat X_M$, write
$\pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_{M-1}:X_M\to X$. Then $(f_M,X_M)$ is
algebraically stable and we call $\pi:(f_M,X_M)\to(f,X)$ a minimal
stabilisation of $(f,X)$ (by blowups) when it exists.}

This terminology is justified by the next theorem, which says that the
final result of the Minimal Stabilisation Algorithm, when it terminates,
has a universal property.

\sourcestatement{Theorem 1.4}{Let $f:X\rat X$ be a rational map on a
surface. If there exists a birational morphism $\rho:(g,Y)\to(f,X)$
stabilising $f$ then any instance of the Minimal Stabilisation Algorithm
terminates in a minimal stabilisation
$\pi:(\widehat f,\widehat X)\to(f,X)$ such that $\rho=\pi\circ\nu$ for
some $\nu:Y\to\widehat X$. It follows that the minimal stabilisation
$(\widehat f,\widehat X)$ is unique for $(f,X)$.}

\sourcestatement{Corollary 1.5}{Let $f:X\rat X$ be a birational map on
a surface. Then there exists a unique minimal stabilisation
$\pi:(\widehat f,\widehat X)\to(f,X)$.}
\begin{proof}
By [7], there exists a birational morphism $\rho:\widetilde X\to X$ which
makes $\widetilde f=\rho^{-1}\circ f\circ\rho$ algebraically stable on
$\widetilde X$. By Theorem 1.4, the minimal stabilisation
$\widehat f:\widehat X\rat\widehat X$ via $\pi:\widehat X\to X$ exists
(uniquely and factors $\rho$).
\end{proof}

\section*{Author's text: 2. Background}
% SOURCE physical 7, printed 52: paragraph introducing Section 2.
For the rest of this article, assume all surfaces are smooth projective
over an algebraically closed field, and rational maps are dominant. An
account of most of the facts below can be found in [17, \S V].

% SOURCE physical 8, printed 53: complete notation and graph context.
Let $X,Y$ be surfaces and $f:X\rat Y$ a rational map. Let $U$ be the
largest (open) set on which $f:U\to Y$ is a morphism, then we define the
indeterminate set as $I(f)=X\setminus U$. Alternatively, these are the
finitely many points at which $f$ cannot be continuously defined. These
are often also called fundamental points.

An irreducible curve $C\subset X$ is exceptional iff $f(C\setminus I(f))$
is a point in $Y$. We define the exceptional set, $\mathcal E(f)$, of $f$
to be the union of all (finitely many) irreducible exceptional curves in
$X$. Denote by $\exc(f)$ the number of irreducible components in
$\mathcal E(f)$.

\sourceheading{Remark 2.1}
In the case of the inverse of a birational map, $I(f^{-1})$ is the proper
transform of $\mathcal E(f)$, or the set of values of $f$ with infinite
preimage. Using this latter definition we generalise the meaning of
$I(f^{-1})$ to any rational map $f$.

Let $f:X\rat Y$ be a rational map of surfaces. The graph of $f$ is the
subvariety
\[
 \Gamma_f=\overline{\{(x,f(x))\in X\setminus I(f)\times Y\}}
 \subset X\times Y
\]
along with projections $\alpha:\Gamma_f\to X$ onto the first factor and
$\beta:\Gamma_f\to Y$ onto the second factor which are proper.
$\Gamma_f$ is irreducible because $X\setminus I(f)$ is.

$I(f)$ is the set of points where $\alpha$ does not have a local inverse.
In particular $\alpha^{-1}:X\setminus I(f)\to\Gamma_f$ is an isomorphism.
For $p\notin I(f)$ we have $\beta(\alpha^{-1}(p))=f(p)$. In general for
any set of points $S\subseteq X$, we may define the total transform of $S$
by $f$ as $f(S)=\beta(\alpha^{-1}(S))$. When
$\varnothing\neq S\subseteq I(f)$ this image has dimension 1.
$\mathcal E(f)\subset X$ is the $\alpha$ projection of the set of points
where $\beta$ is not finite-to-one.

$\Gamma_f$ need not be smooth and it will be more convenient to work with
the minimal smooth desingularisation $\Sigma_f$ of $\Gamma_f$. Abusing
notation slightly, we denote the lifted projections as
$\alpha:\Sigma_f\to X$ and $\beta:\Sigma_f\to Y$. Recall the
Néron--Severi group, $\NS(X)$; when $Y=X$ and $f$ is birational, $\beta$
is also a birational morphism, and one can deduce that
$\exc(\alpha)=\exc(\beta)=\operatorname{rk}\NS(\Sigma_f)-\operatorname{rk}\NS(X)$.

\sourceheading{Remark 2.2}
Equivalently $\Sigma_f$ and $\alpha:\Sigma_f\to X$ can be obtained as the
birational morphism, blowing up $X$, which (minimally) resolves the
indeterminacy of $f$. Once resolved $f:X\rat Y$ will lift through
$\alpha$ to a morphism which is precisely $\beta:\Sigma_f\to Y$.
We obtain a map $\alpha\times\beta:\Sigma_f\to X\times Y$ and one can
check its image is $\Gamma_f$, hence it is a smooth desingularisation which
dominates the minimal one. Since the minimal desingularisation is a
candidate for resolving the indeterminacy we also get a birational morphism
the other direction, meaning the two definitions must agree.

% SOURCE physical 9, printed 54.
\sourceheading{Remark 2.3 (Warning)}
$\Sigma_f$ may contain curves which appear neither in the domain $X$ or
the codomain $Y$, meaning both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ map the curve to a
point. This issue will be rectified in Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 4.6.
For an example, pick any surface with a rational curve $C$ of
self-intersection 0, and construct the birational map which blows up a
point on $C$ to give an exceptional curve $D$, blows up another point of
$D$ to give $E$, but then blows down $C$ followed by $D$. The second curve
$D$ (i.e. its proper transform) is contracted in both the domain and range
of this map, however it can be found in the smooth graph (which is the
intermediate surface containing all three curves).

\sourcestatement{Proposition 2.4 (See [17, \S V 5.3 \& 5.4])}{Let
$f:X\to Y$ be a birational morphism of surfaces. Then $f$ can be written
as a composition of $\exc(f)$ point blowups.}
\textit{Suppose $p\in I(f^{-1})$ and $\pi:Y'\to Y$ be the point blowup of
$p$. Then $f$ factors as $\pi\circ f'$ where $f':X\to Y'$ is a birational
morphism with $\exc(f')=\exc(f)-1$.}

\textit{Otherwise if $p\notin I(f^{-1})$ and $\rho:X'\to X$ is the point
blowup of $f^{-1}(p)$. Then $f$ lifts to a birational morphism
$f'=\pi^{-1}\circ f\circ\rho$ with $\exc(f')=\exc(f)$.}

\sourceheading{Remark 2.5}
Note that Proposition 2.4 does not hold for all rational morphisms, meaning
it can fail if we replace ``birational'' with ``rational'', and consider
$I(f^{-1})$ as defined in Remark 2.1. The second part of the proposition
fails in Example 6.9.

\sourcestatement{Definition 2.6}{Let $f:X\rat Y$ and $g:Y\rat Z$ be
rational maps on surfaces. We say an irreducible curve $C\subset X$ is a
destabilising curve for the composition $g\circ f$ iff
$f(C\setminus I(f))=y\in I(g)$. Equivalently $C\subseteq f^{-1}(y)$ and
$g(y)\supseteq D$ for some irreducible curve $D\subset Z$. We call $D$ an
inverse destabilising curve, and we say that $y$ destabilises the composition
$g\circ f$. We say that the composition $g\circ f$ is locally stable at
$x\in X$ iff $x$ is not contained in any destabilising curve.}

By unravelling the definitions given above, we get the following proposition.

\sourcestatement{Proposition 2.7}{Let $f:X\rat Y$ and $g:Y\rat Z$ be
rational maps. Then
\[
 g(f(x))\supseteq(g\circ f)(x)
\]
with equality if $x$ is not contained in a destabilising curve. Moreover
$z\in g(f(x))$ if and only if $z\in(g\circ f)(x)$ or we can find
$y\in I(g)\cap I(f^{-1})$ destabilising the composition $g\circ f$ where
$z\in g(y)$ and $x\in f^{-1}(y)$.}

% SOURCE physical 10, printed 55: complete definitions and criterion.
\sourcestatement{Definition 2.8}{Let $f:X\rat X$ be a rational map and
let $p,f(p),\ldots,f^{m-1}(p)$ be an orbit in $X$. We say this is a
destabilising orbit iff there is an (indeterminate) $q\in f^{m-1}(p)$ such
that both $f(q)=D$ and $f^{-1}(p)=C$ are curves. Let $N\in\mathbb N$, then
we say the orbit is $N$-eventually destabilising iff there is a closed point
$q\in f^{m-1}(p)$ such that both $f(q)=D$ and $f^{-n}(p)=C$ are curves
for some $n\geq N$.}
\textit{In either destabilising scenario, we say the length of the orbit is
$m$, we call each irreducible component of $C$ a destabilising curve and
each component of $D$ an inverse destabilising curve of $f$.}

\sourcestatement{Definition 2.9}{Let $f:X\rat X$ be a rational map. We
say that $f$ is algebraically stable iff for every $n\geq0$ we have
$(f^n)^*=(f^*)^n$. We say $f$ is $N$-eventually algebraically stable iff
for every $n\geq N$ and $m\geq0$ we have
$(f^{n+m})^*=(f^n)^*(f^m)^*=(f^n)^*(f^*)^m$.}

\sourcestatement{Proposition 2.10 ([7, 1.14], [13])}{Let $f:X\rat X$ be
a rational map. Then $f$ is algebraically stable if and only if $f$ has
no destabilising orbits. Similarly, $f$ is $N$-eventually algebraically
stable if and only if $f$ has no $N$-eventually destabilising orbits.}

This geometric characterisation of algebraic stability can be understood
through Proposition 2.7. One can show that $f^*g^*D-(g\circ f)^*D$ is
supported on destabilising curves for any divisor $D$ and moreover that
the composition $g\circ f$ is stable if and only if $f^*g^*=(g\circ f)^*$.

\section*{Author's text: 3. Minimal Stabilisation}
\sourcestatement{Definition 3.1}{We say that a destabilising orbit
$p,f(p),\ldots,f^{m-1}(p)$ is minimal iff the $p_j=f^{j-1}(p)$ are all
distinct closed points where for $1\leq j<m$ we have $p_j\notin I(f)$,
and for $1<j\leq m$ we have $p_j\notin I(f^{-1})$.}

It is easy to see that the points of a minimal destabilising orbit do not
contain any shorter destabilising orbits and conversely that any
destabilising orbit of minimum length $m$ is minimal, so these must always
exist when $f$ is not algebraically stable. Minimality is less natural for
eventually destabilising orbits. An $N$-eventually destabilising orbit always
possesses a point that constitutes a singleton $N$-eventually destabilising
orbit, which is vacuously minimal.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Proposition 1.2]
First note that by applying Proposition 2.4 ($n$ times), if $\rho$ blows up
all the $p_j$ at least once, then we get a new birational morphism $\nu$
which provides the factorisation $\rho=\pi\circ\nu$. Therefore we will
% SOURCE physical 11, printed 56: proof continues without omission.
proceed to show that $\rho$ does indeed blowup the $p_j$. Let
$\widehat p_j=\rho^{-1}(p_j)$, which a priori may be closed points or
exceptional curves.
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large,column sep=large]
Y \arrow[r,dashed,"g"] \arrow[d,"\rho"'] & Y \arrow[d,"\rho"] \\
X \arrow[r,dashed,"f"] & X
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Suppose not; then there is a largest $m\leq n$ such that $\widehat p_m$
is a closed point in $Y$, so we claim this is indeterminate for $g$. Say
$m=n$ and $f(p_n)=D\subset X$, then $\widehat p_n\in I(g)$ if
$g(\widehat p_n)$ is a curve, for which it is enough to show that
$\rho(g(\widehat p_n))$ is a curve. Indeed
\[
\rho(g(\widehat p_n))=\rho\circ g(\widehat p_n)
=f\circ\rho(\widehat p_n)=f(p_n)=D
\]
is a curve; note that $I(\rho)=\varnothing$ and the last step holds because
$\rho$ is locally an isomorphism at $\widehat p_n$. If $m<n$ then
$p_{m+1}\notin I(f^{-1})$, so the composition $\rho^{-1}\circ f$ is locally
stable at $p_m$, and $\rho$ is locally an isomorphism at $\widehat p_m$
so $(\rho^{-1}\circ f)\circ\rho=g$ is locally stable near
$\widehat p_m$. Therefore
\[
g(\widehat p_m)=\rho^{-1}(f(\rho(\widehat p_m)))=\rho^{-1}(p_{m+1})
\]
which is also a curve by assumption.

Suppose that $k\leq m$ is minimal such that $p_k,\ldots,p_m$ are not
blown up by $\rho$ and either $k=1$ or $k-1$ is blown up by $\rho$. Since
$\rho$ is a local isomorphism over these points, one sees that
$\widehat p_k\mapsto\widehat p_{k+1}\mapsto\cdots\mapsto\widehat p_m$.
To provide a contradiction to the algebraic stability of $g$, we will next
show that this is a destabilising orbit for $g$. We only need to show
that $g^{-1}(p_k)$ is a curve and this is very similar to the case of $p_m$
above.

$\rho$ is locally an isomorphism near $\widehat p_k$. So it is enough to
show that $(f\circ\rho)^{-1}(p_k)$ is a curve. Say $k=1$ and hence
$f^{-1}(p_1)$ contains a curve $C$, then $(f\circ\rho)^{-1}(p_1)$ contains
$\rho^{-1}(C\setminus I(f))$ which is (almost all of) a curve. Otherwise
$k>1$, so $p_{k-1}\notin I(f)$ and the composition $f\circ\rho$ is
algebraically stable over $\rho^{-1}(p_{k-1})$ which is a curve
$\widehat C$. We get that $\rho^{-1}\circ f^{-1}(p_k)=\widehat C$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem 1.4]
Given that $g:Y\rat Y$ dominates $f$ via
$\rho:(g,Y)\to(f,X)=(f_1,X_1)$ we may proceed inductively on $m$ with the
hypothesis that $g:Y\rat Y$ dominates $f_m:X_m\rat X_m$ via
$\nu_m:Y\to X_m$.

If $f_m$ is algebraically stable we are done, otherwise Proposition 1.2
says that because $\pi_m$ blows up a minimal destabilising orbit we have
a $\nu_{m+1}:Y\to X_{m+1}$ which factors $\nu_m$ as
$\nu_m=\pi_m\circ\nu_{m+1}$.
% SOURCE physical 12, printed 57: final proof, all paragraphs and diagram.
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large,column sep=large]
X_{m+1} \arrow[d,"\pi_m"'] & Y \arrow[l,red,"\nu_{m+1}"'] \arrow[dl,"\nu_m"] \\
X_m & {}
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Clearly there is no limit to the number of times we can do this if $f_m$
is never algebraically stable for $m\geq1$. However overall we have shown
that
\[
\rho=\nu_1=\pi_1\circ\nu_2=\pi_1\circ\pi_2\circ\nu_3
=\cdots=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_m\circ\nu_{m+1}=\pi\circ\nu_{m+1}
\]
meaning that $\exc(\rho)\geq m$. Therefore
$\{m\in\mathbb N:f_m\text{ is not AS}\}$ is in fact bounded above,
strictly by $m=M$ say, and whence $f_M$ is algebraically stable. Moreover,
$\rho=\pi\circ\nu$ where we define $\nu=\nu_M$.

We have shown that $\pi$ factors any birational morphism stabilising $f$,
and to finish we apply this to get uniqueness of $(\widehat f,\widehat X)$.
Suppose we proceed in the Minimal Stabilisation Algorithm in two different
ways which produce two (potentially different) models, namely
$\widehat f_1:\widehat X_1\rat\widehat X_1$ via
$\pi_1:\widehat X_1\to X$ and
$\widehat f_2:\widehat X_2\rat\widehat X_2$ via
$\pi_2:\widehat X_2\to X$. By the above we have that
$\pi_1=\pi_2\circ\nu_1$ and $\pi_2=\pi_1\circ\nu_2$. We deduce that
$\nu_1,\nu_2$ are inverse morphisms to each other, providing an
isomorphism not only of surfaces but dynamical systems
$\nu_1:(\widehat f_1,\widehat X_1)\leftrightarrow
(\widehat f_2,\widehat X_2)$, i.e. the following diagram commutes.
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large,column sep=huge]
\widehat X_1
 \arrow[rr,bend right=15,"\nu_1"']
 \arrow[dr,"\pi_1"']
 \arrow[loop left,"\mathrm{id}"']
 & {} & \widehat X_2
 \arrow[ll,bend right=15,"\nu_2"']
 \arrow[dl,"\pi_2"]
 \arrow[loop right,"\mathrm{id}"] \\
 & X & {}
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\end{proof}

original_metadata.title: For 0<q<1, u>0 and coprime n>=2,n prime>0, the n-fermion currents (4.4) realize the SL2(Z)-twisted charged q-difference module with central charges (n,n prime)
original_metadata.author: Mikhail Bershtein; Roman Gonin
original_metadata.source_title: Twisted Representations of Algebra of q-Difference Operators, Twisted q-W Algebras and Conformal Blocks
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The obligation is to construct the twisted Chevalley currents explicitly, although the lattice automorphism is simple only on the full lattice-mode algebra. The proof embeds the q-difference algebra through an index-n sublattice, identifies the restricted charged Fock module and splits a single Clifford current into residue classes, tracking fractional powers and normal-order scalar terms. This representation-theoretic construction is substantially beyond ordinary Lie/Clifford algebra qualifying material.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the nontrivial positive-slope branch of Theorem4.1: 0<q<1, u>0 with positive roots chosen, n>=2 and n prime>0 coprime, sigma=[[m prime,m],[n prime,n]] in SL2(Z). On the full charged n-fermion Clifford module F^{n psi}, the currents (4.4) and H_k^{tw} act as Diff_q with c=n,c prime=n prime and identify the module with M_u^sigma. M_u is the full charged level-one fermion module (direct sum of Fock charge sectors), so this does not assert that the whole space is a single irreducible F_u^sigma. The selected proof is the sublattice proof in Section5, with regular-product context; other bosonic realizations and conformal-block identities are excluded.

original_metadata.title: For separable graded A and sigma-unital graded B, stable homotopy of unbounded Kasparov modules modulo spectral decomposability is identified with KK(A,B) by the bounded transform
original_metadata.author: Jens Kaad
original_metadata.source_title: On the Unbounded Picture of KK-Theory
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The new obligation is injectivity at the unbounded-cycle level: lifting a bounded homotopy alone does not connect its endpoints to the original unbounded operators. The author regularizes and doubles the operators, constructs an explicit rotated homotopy for cycles sharing a phase, and verifies its domain, compactness and graded-commutator requirements. This closes a nontrivial unbounded KK-theory equivalence and requires substantially more than a standard bounded functional-calculus exercise.

original_metadata.title: For g>L>=0, psi-class intersection numbers with the first n-2 exponents summing to at most L satisfy the explicit uniform lower bound lambda(g,L) times the double-factorial approximation
original_metadata.author: Vincent Delecroix; Elise Goujard; Peter Zograf; Anton Zorich
original_metadata.source_title: Uniform Lower Bound for Intersection Numbers of psi-Classes
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The central obligation is to maintain an explicit multiplicative error bound uniformly in the number and distribution of descendant exponents. The proof builds compatible defects for the string, dilaton and Virasoro recursions and uses a coupled induction on the small-exponent sum and the number of zero entries, with separate genus-lowering terms. This is a substantive moduli-space intersection-number estimate, beyond evaluating a few standard correlators or applying the recursion mechanically.

original_metadata.title: For N>=2, angularly separated spectral ratios and nonzero real q,kappa with opposite inside/outside unit-circle magnitudes give absolute convergence of the nonstationary f_N,infinity Ruijsenaars series near its affine ratio origin
original_metadata.author: Edwin Langmann; Masatoshi Noumi; Junichi Shiraishi
original_metadata.source_title: Basic Properties of Non-Stationary Ruijsenaars Functions
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The key obligation is a uniform exponential bound on coefficients indexed by N partitions, despite infinitely many periodic spectral factors and potentially small denominators. The author separates angular and same-period factors, controls their integer exponents by partition inequalities and telescopes the complete product into a bound in total partition size. This provides an actual analytic convergence domain for a formal nonstationary special function and exceeds checking a simple power series by the ratio test.

original_metadata.title: For M,N>=1 over C, the degree-(r-1) associated graded RTT Yangian of the general linear Lie superalgebra on an M-even, N-odd superspace is the enveloping algebra of its polynomial current Lie superalgebra
original_metadata.author: Maxim Nazarov
original_metadata.source_title: Yangian of the General Linear Lie Superalgebra
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The substantive obligation is injectivity of the current-algebra map, which is not obtained by merely taking leading terms in the RTT relations. The author separates every possible relation using tensor evaluation representations, supersymmetrization and independent spectral-parameter polynomials, including the identity-current factors that ordinary matrix tensors cannot directly distinguish. This proves a genuine super-Yangian PBW deformation statement beyond the usual qualifying-exam PBW theorem for finite-dimensional Lie algebras.

original_metadata.title: A closed two-sided pi1-injective hypersurface with nonzero Rosenberg index in a complete spin n-manifold forces infimum scalar curvature <=-n(n-1)tan^2(nd/4) when its width-d neighbourhood has scalar curvature >=n(n-1) and 0<d<2pi/n
original_metadata.author: Rudolf Zeidler
original_metadata.source_title: Width, Largeness and Index Theory
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The obligation is a quantitative negative scalar-curvature bound away from a positively curved band, rather than only a qualitative obstruction to uniformly positive curvature. The author designs a smooth global Callias potential by a truncated Riccati equation, controls it inside and outside the band and forces a uniform operator-square lower bound that contradicts the hypersurface index. This combines a sharp geometric inequality with Hilbert-C*-module index theory beyond standard qualifying Dirac-operator material.

original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The theorem treats arbitrary small groupoids and their rings with enough idempotents, where a global unit and finite-dimensional group algebra cannot be assumed. These compatibility and finiteness obligations go beyond finite-group Frobenius reciprocity or a single induction calculation.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.6 for every real nu>-1. M^(nu) is the projective probability measure on infinite positive-definite complex Hermitian matrices whose N-corner density is the normalized det(X)^(-nu-2N)*exp(-2*Tr(X^-1)) on H^+(N). In the Pickrell–Olshanski–Vershik parametrization, its spectral measure is supported on Omega_0^+: every negative alpha vanishes, all positive alpha_i are nonzero, gamma_2=0, and gamma_1=sum_i alpha_i^+<infinity. The positive parameters form the determinantal process on (0,infinity) with Lebesgue kernel K_infty^nu(x,y)=8/(x*y)*J_nu(8/x,8/y), where J_nu is the exact Bessel kernel of Definition1.5. No infinite-mass inverse-Wishart parameter range, real-matrix analogue or Hua–Pickrell trace result is asserted.

original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The Staeckel one-variable identity does not control the additional curvature terms caused by blocks of dimension greater than one. original_metadata.title: At noncritical affine-sl2 level, the explicit twisted de Rham complex on the punctured line embeds as a shifted subcomplex of current-algebra chains with tensor contragradient Verma coefficients
original_metadata.author: Alexey Slinkin; Alexander Varchenko
original_metadata.source_title: Twisted de Rham Complex on Line and Singular Vectors in sl(2) Verma Modules
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: Compatibility of the de Rham differential with the current-algebra action requires nontrivial affine-Verma identities at every pole order, not just agreement on logarithmic one-forms. The authors prove those identities by evaluating all PBW basis types and controlling higher-current commutator cancellations, then use them in both the finite-point and infinity expansions of the chain map. The injection remains valid at resonant highest weights, while the noncritical level and shifted degrees are essential.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem4.1: z_1,...,z_n are pairwise distinct complex points, U=C minus these points, k,m_1,...,m_n are complex with k+2!=0, kappa=k+2 and m_{n+1}=sum_{j=1}^n m_j-2. V_j is the affine-sl_2 Verma module V(m_j,k-m_j), with the restricted graded contragradient V_j^*. The source current algebra consists of sl_2-valued rational functions regular on U, acting by Laurent expansions at the finite points and by the specified pi automorphism at infinity. The exact maps(4.2)-(4.5) give an injective homomorphism from Omega^bullet(U)[1] with differential d-(1/kappa)*sum_j m_j*dt/(t-z_j) wedge to the Chevalley–Eilenberg chain complex with tensor_{j=1}^{n+1} V_j^* coefficients; the degree-zero and degree-minus-one terms satisfy d*eta^0=eta^1*partial. No irreducibility or nonresonance of the Verma modules is assumed, and no assertion at k=-2 is selected.

original_metadata.title: For a compact connected prequantized Hamiltonian action of a compact connected Lie group, multiplicities near the zero moment-polytope vertex have the exact weakly regular orbifold-sector formula of Theorem 1.2
original_metadata.author: Yiannis Loizides
original_metadata.source_title: Quasi-Polynomials and the Singular [Q,R]=0 Theorem
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof must compute representation multiplicities even when zero is a singular value and the principal cross-section has a nontrivial generic stabilizer. It combines a detailed support analysis of quasi-polynomial contributions with equivariant index localization and stationary phase in a coisotropic normal form. The author identifies all orbifold sectors and curvature terms, then establishes exactness of the asymptotic formula on an entire lattice cone.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.2 with its introduction hypotheses: M compact connected symplectic, G compact connected acting Hamiltonianly with moment map mu_g, G-equivariant Hermitian prequantum line bundle L with compatible curvature -2*pi*i*omega and Kostant condition, and compatible invariant almost complex structure. Otherwise a full-relative-dimensional closed polytope p within Delta containing zero exists, and for a sufficiently nearby weakly regular value xi the exact displayed sector-integral formula holds for every integral (k,lambda) in C_p. Weak regularity means regularity of the principal cross-section moment map into the affine hull I, not regularity of the full G moment map. All Sigma_g, normal denominators, g_L phases, curvature pairing and the factor 1/d for potentially ineffective orbifold charts are retained from the source.

original_metadata.title: In characteristic zero, the constants of the free-associative derivation Delta(X)=0 and Delta(Y)=X^m for m>=2 have the explicit permissible-bracket free generating set of Theorem 4.6
original_metadata.author: Vesselin Drensky; Leonid Makar-Limanov
original_metadata.source_title: Locally Nilpotent Derivations of Free Algebra of Rank Two
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The kernel is infinitely generated, so triangularity of the derivation does not identify either its generators or all possible relations. The author proves a weighted spanning theorem using a noncommutative bracket operation and then reconstructs permissible bracket words from leading monomials. The resulting normal-form and indecomposability argument gives an explicit free basis, going beyond a direct application of freeness for a homogeneous kernel.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete Theorem4.6 proof, the kernel-spanning induction4.2/Corollary4.3 and the permissible-word construction4.5 were read. The author first controls every element killed by a power of the derivation using weighted induction and explicit commutators of the bracket operation, then proves kernel generation by permissible bracketed words. The final proof reconstructs each word root and matching brackets uniquely from its leading monomial and rules out a factorization by lower-weight permissible leading words. Select the explicit homogeneous monomial-derivation kernel for m>=2; the short equal-kernel rigidity theorem3.3 and the known linear Weitzenboeck case are not counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the explicit homogeneous case of Theorem4.6 for a field K of characteristic zero and integer m>=2. Work in the free unitary associative algebra K<X,Y> with Delta(X)=0, Delta(Y)=X^m and T_1=YX-XY. The bracket operation is boxdot(A)=Y*A*X^m-X^m*A*Y. The kernel R_{X^m} is freely generated by X,T_1 and boxdot of the permissible matching-bracket words T_1^{i_1} X^{j_1} ... X^{j_{k-1}} T_1^{i_k} of Lemma4.5, with i_a positive, 0<=j_a<m, and every right matching bracket preceded by T_1. The full source bracketing convention is retained. This does not assert a finite generating set, does not count the m=1 Weitzenboeck case separately, and does not broaden the explicit generator description to an arbitrary polynomial f.

original_metadata.title: Over any commutative ring and for arbitrary alpha,beta, all pathless representatives of one subdivision-algebra coset have the same image under x_(i,j) mapped to t_i
original_metadata.author: Darij Grinberg
original_metadata.source_title: t-Unique Reductions for Mészáros's Subdivision Algebra
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: Pathless straightening is not confluent and the evaluation map does not annihilate the relation ideal on arbitrary polynomials. Combining those restrictions with an injective formal substitution proves uniqueness uniformly over arbitrary commutative coefficient rings.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem2.7 for any commutative ring k,alpha,beta in k and positive integer n. Pathless means a linear combination of monomials with no x_(i,j)*x_(j,k) divisor for i<j<k. This does not assert uniqueness of q itself or D(q)=D(p), and no forkless-basis neighbor is counted.

original_metadata.title: A symmetric Hamburger moment problem with b_(n-1)/b_n<=q<1 eventually has bounded normalized moment/kernel coefficients and the cs-star absolute summability giving an entrywise absolutely convergent reproducing-kernel inverse of its Hankel matrix
original_metadata.author: Christian Berg; Ryszard Szwarc
original_metadata.source_title: Inverse of Infinite Hankel Moment Matrices
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: Infinite Hankel inversion requires absolute control of double sums; finite inverse identities do not justify associating the infinite matrix products. The author proves separate moment and reproducing-kernel coefficient bounds by q-Pochhammer inductions and shows stability under finite initial recurrence changes. Their combination yields superexponential decay of the shifted coefficient-moment products and the strong summability needed for a valid inverse.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.9 for a symmetric Hamburger probability-moment problem with infinite support and all moments, Jacobi diagonal a_n=0, positive recurrence b_n, and b_(n-1)/b_n<=q for some0<q<1 and all sufficiently large n. Retain definitions U_n=s_(2n)/(b_0^2...b_(n-1)^2), V_n=b_0...b_(n-1)*c_n and c_n=sqrt(A_(n,n)), where A is the reproducing-kernel coefficient matrix. U_n,V_n,c_n*sqrt(s_(2n)) are bounded and sum_l c_l*abs(s_(l+m)) is finite for every m>=0. The supplied Lemma2.1 yields AH=HA=I with entrywise absolute convergence. No bounded-operator inverse interpretation on l2, uniqueness among all infinite inverses or polynomial-growth relaxation is added.

original_metadata.title: All intrinsic characteristic classes of a smooth Lie algebroid pull back functorially along every transverse smooth map, without a connectivity condition on its fibers
original_metadata.author: Pedro Frejlich
original_metadata.source_title: Morita Invariance of Intrinsic Characteristic Classes of Lie Algebroids
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The adjoint representation up to homotopy of an inverse-image Lie algebroid is not just the pullback adjoint bundle. The proof constructs a compatible connection that splits off the doubled vertical bundle with matching metric connections and identifies the resulting graded Chern-Simons forms. Transverse normal forms and graph factorization then extend the exact identity from submersions to arbitrary transverse maps.

original_metadata.author: Sergey M. Zagorodnyuk
original_metadata.source_title: The Inverse Spectral Problem for Jacobi-Type Pencils
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The inverse construction must recover a real symmetric five-diagonal matrix from a generally non-symmetric polynomial-domain operator, while controlling the positivity of its second subdiagonal. This generalized inverse spectral problem exceeds the ordinary three-term Favard correspondence.

original_metadata.author: Kohei Iwaki; Axel Saenz

original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof must add the residue at the double turning point to the differential recursion and relate its principal specialization to both logarithmic isomonodromy equations. This all-orders construction exceeds computing initial WKB coefficients or applying topological recursion formally.

original_metadata.title: Conformally perturbed ordinary and opposite-algebra twisted spectral triples for ergodic positive-dimensional compact Lie actions with a self-adjoint C1 factor
original_metadata.author: Farzad Fathizadeh; Olivier Gabriel
original_metadata.source_title: On the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet Theorem and Conformally Twisted Spectral Triples for C*-Dynamical Systems
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The construction must control two mutually conjugated differential operators on a shared dense core and prove uniform relative bounds through a conformal deformation. It also preserves weak-Schatten summability using the ergodic representation multiplicity bound and a resolvent factorization, while an opposite-algebra twist cancels the unbounded derivative part of the right commutator. These operator-domain and noncommutative geometric obligations exceed an ordinary compact-resolvent or bounded-commutator exercise.

proof_review.note: Complete4.1 spectral/twisted-spectral construction and all essential analytic3.2-3.8 support read. Peter-Weyl finite-component diagonalization gives essential self-adjointness at u=0; orthogonality of conformally transformed exact/coexact image closures controls d_u and d_u*, and the six-term uniform relative-bound estimate propagates a common core/domain by Kato-Rellich. The ergodic multiplicity bound compares unperturbed eigenvalues with the group Hodge operator, while the resolvent factorization preserves the weak-Schatten n+ ideal along u. Explicit left commutator and right twisted-commutator computations cancel all unbounded derivative terms, and domain preservation/parity are verified. Standard Peter-Weyl, multiplicity theorem, Kato-Rellich and compact-Lie-group Weyl summability are cited background. Standing self-adjointness h=h* from the definition of K_u is retained, although the final theorem abbreviates it as h in A1. No Euler characteristic or neighboring Hodge consequence is separately counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: The positive-dimensional case n=dim G>=1 of author4.1. A unital C*-algebra with strongly continuous ergodic compact Lie group G action and unique invariant trace; h=h* in the action-C1 algebra, u in[0,1]. On GNS(A,phi0) tensor exterior(g*), K_u right-multiplies degree-k coefficients by exp((n/2-k)hu), D_u=K_u dK_-u+K_-u d*K_u has its unique self-adjoint extension from the common C1-form core. The left ordinary and right opposite-algebra beta-twisted triples (beta(a)=exp(hu)a exp(-hu)) are even and n+-summable, with source-defined dense bounded-commutator algebra. No non-self-adjoint factor or claim at n=0 is selected.

original_metadata.title: Diffeological differential forms on orbit spaces equal basic forms when the Lie group identity component acts properly
original_metadata.author: Yael Karshon; Jordan Watts
original_metadata.source_title: Basic Forms and Orbit Spaces: a Diffeological Approach
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The quotient may have singular stabilizers and be non-Hausdorff, so pointwise equality of orbits does not provide a smooth group-valued relation between plots. The proof combines a countable-component Baire argument with slice induction on group dimension and a fixed-point velocity comparison for compact connected stabilizers. It also proves the pullback inverse is smooth in the functional diffeology, beyond the classical free proper quotient argument.

proof_review.note: Complete1.1 proof and newSections3-5 support read: pullback injection/basicity, functional-diffeology inverse, quotient-in-stages correspondence, component-coset closedness and Baire density, exponential averaging velocity comparison at a fixed point, slice associated-bundle reduction and induction on group dimension. The plot criterion for descending forms and proper slice theorem are established cited background. All quotient/functional diffeology definitions are bundled. original_metadata.statement_scope: Smooth Lie group G action on manifold M, quotient M/G with quotient diffeology and form spaces with standard functional diffeology. original_metadata.title: Every finite-dimensional real semisimple Lie algebra has a rational form carrying rational forms of all its finite-dimensional real representations

original_metadata.source_title: Hyperkähler Manifolds of Curves in Twistor Spaces

original_metadata.author: Yuri Bazlov; Arkady Berenstein

original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs an explicit automorphism of the monomial-group algebra from parity-dependent root-system cocycles and finite diagonal idempotent factors. original_metadata.source_title: Center of Twisted Graded Hecke Algebras for Homocyclic Groups
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof embeds the deformation in a twisted Laurent crossed product and computes the image of a new multipartite central element through a cancellation indexed by nonadjacent subsets of a cyclic graph. Root-of-unity products and the exceptional cyclic endpoint cocycle factor control the generator images; a filtered-symbol argument then proves that these exhaust the center, beyond merely checking centrality of displayed elements.

original_metadata.title: Level-k quasi-Hamiltonian prequantization criterion for the prescribed-conjugacy-class PU(p) surface component, p an odd prime, with orbifold descent at regular identity value
original_metadata.author: Derek Krepski
original_metadata.source_title: Prequantization of the Moduli Space of Flat PU(p)-Bundles with Prescribed Boundary Holonomies
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof separates the lifted component into ordinary conjugacy factors and a finite central quotient of barycentric conjugacy classes. It computes invariant flag-manifold cohomology and the mod-two Stiefel-Whitney obstruction on that quotient, then combines the resulting torsion cancellation with fusion and relative integral cohomology to obtain a necessary and sufficient level criterion.
